answer: A stake bond turns identity creation into a priced commitment: before an agent can earn, it locks a deposit that a beacon of honest peers can slash if the identity proves to be a copy. Like a vine that only climbs a mesa it can grip, a Sybil farm must fund every fake separately, so a thousand clones cost a thousand bonds. Honest agents keep their deposit safe, while attackers pay up front for identities that die the moment they are exposed.
